tasks.title: Define SQLAlchemy Models and Migration for Group and Book
tasks.description: Create the SQLAlchemy ORM models for `t_user_group` and `t_user_book` based on the PRD. Establish the necessary relationships, such as the link between a book and its group, and a group to its owner. Generate an Alembic migration script to create these new tables in the database.
tasks.details: Create `moneynote/models/group.py` and `moneynote/models/book.py`. The `Group` model should map to `t_user_group` and include columns like `name`, `owner_id`, `default_currency_code`. The `Book` model should map to `t_user_book` with columns like `name`, `group_id`, `default_currency_code`. After creating the models, run `alembic revision --autogenerate` to create the migration script and review it for correctness.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the Alembic migration (`alembic upgrade head`) on a test database to confirm the tables and columns are created correctly. Manually inspect the database schema to verify it matches the PRD specifications.

tasks.title: Define Pydantic Schemas for Group and Book Operations
tasks.description: Create all necessary Pydantic schemas for handling group and book creation requests and responses, as specified in the PRD.
tasks.details: In the `moneynote/schemas/` directory, create `group.py` and `book.py`. Implement the following schemas: `GroupAddForm`, `BookAddForm`, `BookAddByTemplateForm`, `BookAddByBookForm`. Also, create response schemas like `Group` and `Book` to be used for serializing the data returned by the API endpoints.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests can be written to validate the schemas with sample valid and invalid data to ensure they raise appropriate validation errors.

tasks.title: Implement Basic CRUD Functions for Group and Book
tasks.description: Create the data access layer functions for creating and querying `Group` and `Book` entities.
tasks.details: Create `moneynote/crud/crud_group.py` and `moneynote/crud/crud_book.py`. Implement functions like `create_group(db, group_in)`, `get_group_by_name_and_owner(db, name, owner_id)`, `create_book(db, book_in)`, and `get_book_by_name_and_group(db, name, group_id)`. These functions will encapsulate the direct SQLAlchemy database interactions.
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for each CRUD function, using a mock database session to verify that the correct SQLAlchemy methods are called with the expected parameters.

tasks.title: Implement Bulk/Copy CRUD Functions for Book Entities
tasks.description: Implement efficient, bulk-operation CRUD functions for copying categories, tags, and payees from one book to another, as required for the copy and template features.
tasks.details: In the existing CRUD files (`crud_category.py`, `crud_tag.py`, `crud_payee.py`), add new functions that perform bulk inserts. For the copy feature, implement a function like `copy_all_from_book(db, source_book_id, new_book_id)` that uses an `INSERT INTO ... SELECT FROM ...` SQL statement for maximum efficiency. For the template feature, create a function that accepts a list of Pydantic objects and performs a bulk insert.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests should be written to verify these functions. For the copy function, set up a source book with entities in a test database, run the function, and assert that the entities have been correctly duplicated for the new book.

tasks.title: Implement `POST /books` Endpoint (Create from Scratch)
tasks.description: Implement the API endpoint and service logic for creating a new, empty book within the user's active group.
tasks.details: Create `moneynote/routers/books.py` and `moneynote/services/book_service.py`. In the service, create a function `create_empty_book` that validates the uniqueness of the book name within the group and uses `crud_book.create_book` to persist it. In the router, define the `POST /books` endpoint that depends on the current user, validates the `BookAddForm` payload, and calls the service function.
tasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test that sends a request to `POST /books`. Verify a `201 Created` response is returned and check the database to confirm that a new, empty book has been created and associated with the correct group.

tasks.title: Implement `POST /books/template` Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement the API endpoint and transactional service logic for creating a new book from a system-defined template.
tasks.details: In `book_service.py`, create a function `create_book_from_template`. This function will start a database transaction, create the book record, load the specified template from the `data_loader_service`, and use the bulk CRUD functions (from task 24) to populate categories, tags, and payees. The entire operation must be atomic. Add the `POST /books/template` endpoint to `books.py` router.
tasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test for the happy path (valid template ID) and negative path (invalid template ID). For the happy path, assert the `201 Created` response and verify that the new book and all its associated entities from the template exist in the database.

tasks.title: Implement `POST /groups` Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement the API endpoint and transactional service logic for creating a new group, which includes the creation of a default book from a template.
tasks.details: Create `moneynote/routers/groups.py` and `moneynote/services/group_service.py`. The service logic must be transactional. It will validate the group name, create the `Group` entity, create the user-group ownership relation, and then call the `book_service.create_book_from_template` logic (from task 26) to create the initial book. Add the `POST /groups` endpoint to the new router.
tasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test that sends a valid `GroupAddForm`. Assert a `201 Created` response and verify in the database that the group, the user-group relation, the default book, and all the book's template-based entities have been created correctly within a single transaction.

tasks.title: Implement `POST /books/copy` Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement the API endpoint and transactional service logic for creating a new book by copying the structure of an existing book.
tasks.details: In `book_service.py`, create a function `create_book_by_copying`. It must validate the source book's existence and user's access. The function will be transactional: it creates the new book record, then uses the efficient `INSERT...SELECT` CRUD functions (from task 24) to duplicate all categories, tags, and payees from the source book to the new book. Add the `POST /books/copy` endpoint to the `books.py` router.
tasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test. First, create a source book with several categories/tags. Then, call `POST /books/copy`. Assert the `201 Created` response and verify the new book's structure is an exact duplicate of the source book's structure in the database.

tasks.title: Write Integration Tests for Group and Basic Book Creation
tasks.description: Write a comprehensive suite of integration tests for the `POST /groups` and `POST /books` endpoints, covering both happy paths and error conditions.
tasks.details: In `tests/`, create `test_groups.py` and `test_books.py`. For `POST /groups`, test successful creation, duplicate name conflict (409), and bad request (400). For `POST /books`, test successful creation of an empty book, duplicate name conflict (409), and bad request (400). Use a test client and a dedicated test database for all tests.
tasks.testStrategy: These are the tests themselves. Execution will be via `pytest`. Each test case should clean up after itself to ensure test isolation.

tasks.title: Write Integration Tests for Advanced Book Creation
tasks.description: Write a comprehensive suite of integration tests for the `POST /books/template` and `POST /books/copy` endpoints.
tasks.details: In `tests/test_books.py`, add tests for the advanced creation methods. For `POST /books/template`, test with a valid `templateId` and an invalid one (404). For `POST /books/copy`, test with a valid source `bookId` and an invalid/inaccessible one (404). Verify the integrity of the created data in the database for all successful cases.
tasks.testStrategy: These are the tests themselves. Execution will be via `pytest`. The tests will require setting up prerequisite data (e.g., a source book to copy from) before making the API call.
